pharm: Long-acting organic nitrate; the major active metabolite of isosorbide dinitrate. Releases nitric oxide to relax vascular smooth muscle, predominantly venodilation, reducing cardiac preload.
quick: IR 20 mg PO BID (7 h apart); ER 30-120 mg PO once daily
May take with or without food
summary: Isosorbide mononitrate is a long-acting organic nitrate for the prevention and treatment of angina pectoris due to coronary artery disease. It is NOT for aborting an acute anginal attack (onset too slow - use sublingual nitroglycerin for that). Dosing uses a nitrate-free interval to prevent tolerance: immediate-release is 20 mg twice daily with the two doses 7 hours apart; extended-release is once daily. It is contraindicated with PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) and the soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator riociguat due to severe hypotension. Headache is the most common side effect.
indications: Prevention of angina pectoris due to coronary artery disease
Treatment (prophylaxis) of chronic stable angina pectoris

dosage.t: Twice daily, with the two doses 7 hours apart
dosage.n: e.g., 8 a.m. and 3 p.m.; asymmetric dosing gives a nitrate-free interval to limit tolerance; start 5 mg if very small stature, increase to >=10 mg by day 2-3
Swallow whole; do not crush/chew ER tablets; titrate after several days
Dosage adjustments not necessary for age or altered hepatic/renal function

admin: Use the asymmetric twice-daily (7-hour interval) schedule for immediate-release to provide a daily nitrate-free interval and prevent tolerance
Take extended-release tablets once daily, swallowed whole - do not crush or chew
Do not use to relieve an acute anginal attack (onset is too slow)
Do not stop abruptly - taper to avoid rebound angina/coronary vasospasm
May take with or without food
moa: Releases nitric oxide (NO) in vascular smooth muscle, activating guanylate cyclase to increase cyclic GMP, causing smooth-muscle relaxation. Venodilation predominates, promoting peripheral venous pooling and reducing venous return and left-ventricular end-diastolic pressure (preload); arteriolar dilation reduces afterload; coronary arteries also dilate. The net effect lowers myocardial oxygen demand.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to isosorbide mononitrate or other nitrates
Concurrent PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) - severe hypotension/syncope/MI
Concurrent riociguat (soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator) - hypotension
relative: Acute myocardial infarction or congestive heart failure (benefit not established; effects hard to terminate)

preg: Animal studies showed no fetal harm, but there are no adequate well-controlled human studies; use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether isosorbide mononitrate is excreted in human milk; exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman.
renal: No dosage adjustment is necessary for patients with altered renal function.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is necessary for patients with altered hepatic function.

major: PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) - contraindicated; profound hypotension
moderate: Calcium channel blockers (marked symptomatic orthostatic hypotension - may need dose adjustment)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol shows additive vasodilatory/hypotensive effects - avoid.
interactions.diagnostics: High-dose nitrates can rarely cause methemoglobinemia; no routine lab monitoring required.

common: Headache (most frequent; lessens after first days)

monitoring: Blood pressure (including orthostatic) and heart rate
Frequency and severity of anginal episodes
Headache response (often improves with continued use)
Adherence to the nitrate-free interval (to detect/avoid tolerance)
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed - the timing (7-hour gap for twice-daily, or once daily for the long-acting form) keeps the drug working
This will NOT relieve a sudden angina attack - use your short-acting (sublingual) nitrate for that
Headache is common at first and usually fades; do not stop the medicine for it
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to avoid dizziness; sit or lie down if you feel faint
Never take erectile-dysfunction drugs (sildenafil/tadalafil/vardenafil) with nitrates - this can cause dangerous blood pressure drops
Do not stop suddenly; tell your doctor if angina worsens
pk: IR ~1 h after first dose (antianginal effect)
IR at least 7 h after the second dose; ER ~24 h
pearls: Active metabolite of isosorbide dinitrate with ~100% bioavailability and no first-pass effect
The 7-hour-apart twice-daily schedule (or once-daily ER) provides a nitrate-free interval that prevents tolerance
Not for acute angina - too slow in onset; reserve sublingual nitroglycerin for attacks
Absolutely avoid PDE-5 inhibitors and riociguat - life-threatening hypotension
Benefit in acute MI and CHF is not established and effects cannot be terminated quickly - use cautiously if at all
Do not discontinue abruptly to avoid rebound vasospasm
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember, but maintain the proper interval; if it is close to the next dose, skip it and resume your schedule. Do not double up. Keeping the daily nitrate-free period matters more than perfect timing.
overdose: Overdose causes vasodilation, venous pooling, reduced cardiac output, and hypotension - manifesting as throbbing headache, confusion, fever, vertigo, palpitations, visual disturbance, nausea/vomiting, syncope, dyspnea, diaphoresis, bradycardia/heart block, and rarely seizures and death. Treat by elevating the legs, expanding central volume (IV fluids), and supportive care; methemoglobinemia is treated with IV methylene blue. Avoid vasoconstrictors that may worsen ischemia.
